verdicts.evidence: c3ref: 'Every new database connection defaults to having the auto-checkpoint enabled with a threshold of 1000 or SQLITE_DEFAULT_WAL_AUTOCHECKPOINT pages.'

verdicts.claim: SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_NOOP and PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(NOOP) checkpoint zero frames and only return the counters. Both were added in SQ
verdicts.evidence: 3.51.0 release (On 2025-11-04): 'Add the PRAGMA wal_checkpoint=NOOP; command and the SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_NOOP argument for sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2().'

verdicts.claim: SQLite's WAL-reset bug was found and fixed on 2026-03-03 by SQLite developer Dan. It is likely present in every release from 3.7
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'On 2026-03-03, one of the SQLite developers (Dan) found and fixed... 3.7.0 (2010-07-21) through 3.51.2 (2026-01-09). It is fixed in version 3.51.3 (2026-03-13)... Backports... 3.44.6 and 3.50.7.'

verdicts.claim: Antithesis caught it in 15 minutes on SQLite 3.51.2 with a generic concurrent write-and-checkpoint workload, and its run on 3.51.3
verdicts.evidence: Antithesis: 'I had it get SQL 3.51.2 – still buggy... On my first run, Antithesis caught the bug in 15 mins... repeated the exercise with 3.51.3... the run came back green.'

verdicts.claim: Phil Eaton (2026-08-23) lost writes and corrupted a file within seconds using a 100-line C program, only the public API, a large mm
verdicts.evidence: Eaton (August 23, 2026): 'reproduce the race with a 100-line C workload, getting both lost writes and a corrupted database file within seconds using only the public SQLite API'; code sets 'PRAGMA mmap_size=1073741824'.

verdicts.claim: SQLite first said its developers could not reproduce the bug without a test hook, and added a note on 2026-08-24 about Eaton's rep
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'Without that code hack, the problem has never been observed... UPDATE: 2026-08-24 → Phil Eaton has devised a reproducer that does not involve using the special testing code hack.'

verdicts.claim: Litestream v0.5.x checkpoints in three tiers. PASSIVE when the WAL reaches min-checkpoint-page-count (default 1000, about 4 MB).
verdicts.evidence: Litestream guide: 'min-checkpoint-page-count: 1000 # Default: ~4MB', 'checkpoint-interval: 1m', 'truncate-page-n: 121359 # Default: ~500MB', 'v0.5.15 ... first attempts a PASSIVE checkpoint', 'truncate-page-n: 0 # Disable TRUNCATE checkpoints'.

verdicts.claim: better-sqlite3 advises a watchdog for apps with concurrent readers: every 5 seconds, stat the -wal file and run wal_checkpoint(RES
verdicts.evidence: performance.md: setInterval(fs.stat('foobar.db-wal' ...) ... if stat.size > someUnacceptableSize db.pragma('wal_checkpoint(RESTART)') ..., 5000).

verdicts.claim: David Crawshaw hit this with 36 connections and about 1000 writes per second. Setting PRAGMA wal_autocheckpoint=0 on every connect
verdicts.evidence: Forum (Crawshaw): '36 connections open from the same process, about 1000 writes per second' ... 'wal_autocheckpoint=0; on every connection resolves the issue and lets PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(RESTART); succeed reliably.'

verdicts.evidence: Register: 'in August 2025 those backups began detecting database corruption, repeatedly'; 'six months of hunting'; 'Tailscale's decision to perform manual checkpoints was a rare exception'. Techzine: checkpointing 'aggressively'.
